excerpts.text: # How Tall is Mt Elbert? Unraveling the Height of Colorado’s Greatest 14er

The most ‘official’ elevation is provided by the United States Geological Survey (USGS). Their most recent data from 2002 puts [Mt. Elbert at 14,440 feet](https://thenextsummit.org/colorado-14ers/hiking-mount-elbert/) (4,401 meters) above sea level.

For example, Mt Elbert’s official elevation was listed as [14,433 feet until 2002](http://www.skyrunner.com/story/coheights.htm), when the USGS released updated maps based on improved methodologies. They showed the peak was actually seven feet taller than previously thought, bringing the official elevation to 14,440 feet where it has remained ever since.

assessment.rationale: Spans 17, 36, 37 extract the USGS elevation values: 14,440 feet (post-2002 update) and note the prior value was 14,433 feet. No span mentions 14,494 feet or a 2001 USGS table.
assessment.provenance_note: Source records 14,440 ft as the current USGS official figure; 14,433 ft as the prior figure. 14,494 ft is not stated.

excerpts.text: **Mount Elbert** is the [highest summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mountain_peaks_of_the_Rocky_Mountains#Highest_prominent_summits "List of mountain peaks of the Rocky Mountains") of the [Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains") of North America. With an [elevation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elevation "Elevation") of 14,440 ft (4,400 m), it is also the highest point in the [U.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado") and the second-highest summit in the [contiguous United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contiguous_United_States "Contiguous United States") after [Mount Whitney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Whitney "Mount Whitney"), which is slightly taller. The [ultra-prominent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra-prominent_peak "Ultra-prominent peak") [fourteener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteener "Fourteener") is the highest peak in the [Sawatch Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawatch_Range "Sawatch Range"), as well as the highest point in the entire [Mississippi River drainage basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River#Watershed "Mississippi River"). Mount Elbert is located in [San Isabel National Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Isabel_National_Forest "San Isabel National Forest"), 12.1 mi (19.4 km) southwest ([bearing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_bearing "Absolute bearing") 223°) of the city of [Leadville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leadville,_Colorado "Leadville, Colorado") in [Lake County, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_County,_Colorado "Lake County, Colorado").[[4]](#cite_note-NGS-4)[[3]](#cite_note-PB-3)[[5]](#cite_note-GNIS-5)[[a]](#cite_note-7)

Originally measured as 14,433 feet (4,399 m) in height, Mount Elbert's elevation was later adjusted to 14,440 feet (4,400 m) following a re-evaluation of mapped elevations, which sparked protests. The actual change was made in 1988 as a result of the [North American Vertical Datum of 1988](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Vertical_Datum_of_1988 "North American Vertical Datum of 1988"); it seems the original measurement resulted from the Sea Level Datum of 1929.[[8]](#cite_note-Elbert-9)[[17]](#cite_note-18)[[16]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEnright200912-17) A matter of some contention arose after the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression") over the heights of Elbert and its neighbor [Mount Massive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Massive "Mount Massive"), which differ in elevation by only 12 feet (3.7 m).

excerpts.text: Results: Mt Elbert summit is 14,439.45ft +/-0.04ft (NAD83 2011 Epoch 2010 NAVD88 Geoid 18)

Mount Elbert was first surveyed by the USGS in 1894 when a monument was placed on the summit (source – NGS datasheet <https://www.ngs.noaa.gov/cgi-bin/ds_mark.prl?PidBox=KL0637> ). In 1906 it was surveyed again at 14,421ft, with nearby Mt Massive surveyed at 14,424ft, meaning Mt Massive was thought to be the state highpoint then.

According to the NGS datasheet for the Mt Elbert monument (<https://www.ngs.noaa.gov/cgi-bin/ds_mark.prl?PidBox=KL0637>) USGS conducted another survey in 1953 using traditional leveling methods, and found Mt Elbert 14,433ft (NGVD29).
In 1993 the USGS updated the vertical datum for the US to NAVD88, and this resulted in the elevation of Mt Elbert being shifted to 14,440ft, though no additional ground survey was conducted.
